subject: PO vs Card — Procurement next steps / Marketplace interest
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@finservinc.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 14:32:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: PO vs card and procurement path

Hi Emma — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment:

Summary from call:
- FinServ sizing: starting with 4 production endpoints, expected to ramp to ~12 within 6 months.
- Primary constraints: AP prefers Purchase Order (PO) and they have a vendor onboarding process.
- Marketplace: you asked whether we can be purchased via the major cloud marketplace (Azure Marketplace / AWS Marketplace) — short answer: yes, we support marketplace purchases but SKU/catalog listing may take extra lead time.

Immediate asks from your side:
1) Who in procurement should we send the vendor onboarding packet to? (W-9, insurance cert, contact info)
2) Confirm whether net-30 is required or if a credit card pilot could be used to accelerate initial usage while the PO is processed.

Attachments: pricing_sheet_v2.pdf (list pricing/tiers), SOW-draft.docx (initial scope).

Next steps (proposed):
- I will send a single vendor packet and W-9 to procurement once you confirm contact.
- We can enable a short pilot on card to unblock dev work while legal/procurement runs the PO path — if AP policy allows.
- If marketplace purchase is preferred, I can loop in our marketplace ops to start listing and provide an estimated timeline.

Would love to get procurement contact and preferred path by end of this week so we can set expectations internally.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0198

Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:12:21 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: PO vs card and procurement path

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from my side:

- Procurement contact: procurement@finservinc.com (I copied them on this thread) — they own vendor onboarding and payment terms.
- AP policy: our default is PO + net-30 for new vendors. We sometimes do a corporate card for pilots if the finance manager signs off, but that requires a short memo and limit to $5k.
- Marketplace: yes, we'd prefer marketplace if possible because it streamlines approval, but our procurement team will need the marketplace listing and SKU info to proceed.

Ill ask procurement for the vendor onboarding packet and expected timeline (usually 2-4 weeks once paperwork is complete).

Emma
Sr. Product Manager | FinServ Inc.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: procurement@finservinc.com
Cc: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@finservinc.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 12:05:40 -0700
Subject: Intro + vendor docs & options for PO vs card

Hi Procurement team — nice to e-meet you. Emma looped you in. Quick intro: Im Marissa, AE at Redwood Inference. We had a discovery call with Emma about using Redwood for low-latency inference in a few production routes.

To make this as painless as possible, here are the two commercial paths we commonly use:

1) PO (recommended for larger, long-term deals):
- Submit vendor onboarding form + W-9 + insurance cert.
- We sign standard MSA and SOW; net-30 is supported.
- Typical procurement timeline: 2-6 weeks depending on legal review.

2) Credit card pilot (accelerate onboarding):
- Short-term card-based pilot (up to $5k) while PO is routed.
- We can set usage caps and billing alerts; pilot converts to PO once paperwork is complete.

Marketplace option: we can provide SKU and listing metadata to the FinServ procurement team; marketplace purchases can often be processed faster but require catalog setup (estimate 3-4 weeks once initiated).

I attached our pricing sheet and draft SOW earlier; happy to attach a W-9 and our standard vendor packet if youre ready. Next steps I propose:
- Procurement confirms preferred path (PO vs card vs marketplace).
- If PO: procurement returns completed vendor_onboarding_form.pdf and any required legal redlines.
- If card: we enable a trial account and Ill coordinate usage limits with Logan (CC'd).

Happy to set a 30-min procurement sync this week if that helps.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

--
Attachments referenced previously: pricing_sheet_v2.pdf, SOW-draft.docx

Hi Marissa and Emma,

Thanks for the overview. Im the procurement manager for FinServ. Please find attached our vendor onboarding form (vendor_onboarding_form.pdf). To start vendor setup we need:
- Completed onboarding form (attached)
- Company W-9 or W-8 (as applicable)
- Certificate of Insurance (COI)
- Bank details for ACH (we can also process via PO once vendor is approved)

Terms: we generally do net-30 with standard MSA; we can discuss alternate terms case-by-case. If you prefer a card-based pilot to accelerate the evaluation, please send a short memo and a limit request (we typically cap pilots at $5k).

Please return the completed form and docs; once received, onboarding typically takes 7-14 business days.

Regards,
